methods: Verified SHA-256, byte size, PDF metadata and page count before catalog comparison.
Rendered every page in source order (28 FOIA pages at 120 DPI; one IPP-notice page at 180 DPI) and visually inspected the complete sequence.

Checked embedded PDF text page-by-page. The 28-page FOIA packet is image-only; rendered-page visual transcription was used where native extraction was empty. The IPP notice has embedded text and was checked against its rendered page.
Compared both supplied SHA-256 values against the published catalogs and preserved the original supplied filenames as provenance.
Kept personnel/privacy material separate from public environmental evidence and did not infer environmental findings from employment records.

records.status: fully reviewed; excluded from public environmental catalog
records.pageCoverage: all 28 pages rendered and visually reviewed in order; no unreadable page
records.finding: Pages 1–24 and 27–28 are City of Cadillac personnel records for Jeffrey Dietlin: salary and compensation memoranda, payroll-change forms, training certificates, vehicle-policy acknowledgements, a performance note, promotion correspondence, a key receipt and redacted references. Page 5 is a handwritten July 10, 2018 thank-you that refers to sewage blow-back resolution during a June 26 manhole/new sewer-line project and site restoration. Pages 25–26 are an April 2, 2008 Director of Utilities application and resume. They state, as applicant/employee background, prior operation of a 3.2 MGD Class B tertiary wastewater plant and a 2.5 MGD groundwater-remediation plant, plus duties involving plant operations, wastewater laboratory work, biosolids application, capital/budget work and NPDES compliance.
records.boundary: The capacity, duties and upgrade statements are self-reported employment materials, not an agency determination, permit, measured operating record, analytical result, receiving ticket, invoice, violation finding or proof of a PFAS pathway. Salary, performance, driver-license and reference material is not republished in the public environmental catalog.

records.status: fully reviewed; exact duplicate of existing canonical IPP record
records.pageCoverage: page 1 text-extracted, rendered and visually checked
records.finding: The City notice lists 2024 local Industrial Pretreatment Permit exceedances: Rec Boats Holding (Copper, Cyanide and Zinc in Q1); AAR Mobility Systems (Cyanide in Q3–Q4 and Cadmium in Q1–Q2); ARVCO Container (Copper in all four quarters); Cadillac Castings (Zinc Q1, Cadmium Q1–Q2, Silver Q1, Copper Q2 and Molybdenum all four quarters); FIAMM Technologies (Copper Q1 and Q4); Hutchinson (Copper Q1, Q2 and Q4); and MI Rubber Products (Copper all four quarters). The notice states that these categorical-industry exceedances were not known violations by the Cadillac WWTP and that no known environmental impact to the Clam River or Muskegon River watershed was identified (page 1).
records.boundary: This is a municipal public notice of local IPP exceedances. It is not a finding that the WWTP violated its NPDES permit, not a PFAS result and not proof of environmental impact or no impact beyond the notice's stated knowledge.
records.duplicateBasis: The supplied file is byte-identical to the existing canonical record: same 119,427 bytes and SHA-256. No second asset, catalog card or timeline event was created.

queueDecision: The public notice is already published under the canonical IPP record. The FOIA packet is fully reviewed and retained as local provenance/audit material but is not published as an environmental evidence record because it is a redacted personnel file. Its limited plant-role context is tied to existing process, laboratory, biosolids and compliance catalogs without upgrading self-reported statements into independent findings.
evidentiaryBoundary: This intake adds no new environmental event, receiving-history entry, invoice, analytical result, violation determination or groundwater-pathway proof.
